reasoning_notes.reasoning: A middle wage balances margin and the chance of winning labor against an unknown rival offer.
With equal revenue and no labor when underbid, matching the lowest wage maximizes profit; zero wins only if A also bids zero, yielding a split at maximum margin.
Matching my profitable opening wage preserves the chance to split labor if C matches, while undercutting would reduce profit if C stays at zero.
A earned 10 at wage 10; bidding above 0 against that observed wage would only reduce my profit if I win. Keep the low offer and reassess after the next public result.
C has offered 0 twice, so holding 10 preserves 10 profit while monitoring for a change.
A has bid 10 twice. Matching secures half the labor at a profit of 5; undercutting earns less per unit, while bidding higher sacrifices profit if A repeats.
Matching C’s 10 preserves half the labor and earns 5; undercutting by 1 wins the unit for 9, while higher wages lose it. With six rounds remaining, matching avoids escalating wages.
A has held at 10, and matching earns C half the labor while undercutting would sacrifice margin. Keep matching unless A changes its wage.
Matching 10 splits the labor and earns 5, more than conceding or raising the wage. C has matched 10 for two rounds, so hold and observe.
A has bid 10 for the last two rounds, and matching earns C 5 while underbidding sacrifices profit. With five rounds left, keep matching unless A changes its wage.
Matching C’s consistent wage preserves half the labor at a positive margin; undercutting sacrifices margin, while raising risks losing the pool.

Matching A earns 5 if A stays at 10; undercutting by one would earn 9 if A stays, but risks earning nothing if A matches or raises. With four recent rounds at 10 and five rounds left, match to preserve the tie and reassess next round.
Matching C preserves the current split and earns 5; undercutting by 1 wins the unit but earns 9, so I should undercut to improve my share.
Matching the established wage preserves half the labor and earns 5; undercutting sacrifices margin, while bidding higher yields negative profit.
C has matched 10 for several rounds. I undercut to 9 last round, so hold 9 to win if C stays at 10 while retaining a positive margin.
A has held at 10 for five rounds. Matching preserves half the labor at a 10-unit margin; bidding higher would sacrifice profit per unit.

C raised its offer to 10 after my undercut, so matching wins half the labor for profit 5; undercutting again yields at most a small gain if C holds, while risking a losing response. With two rounds left, match and reassess.
A bid 9 after repeatedly bidding 10, so matching 10 wins the full unit and earns 10. A lower bid earns nothing; a higher bid would cut my profit.
Final round: matching 10 secures half the labor for profit 5; undercutting to 9 risks a response and yields only 11 if C stays at 10.
A returned to 10 after bidding 9; matching earns half the pool at a profit of 5. A lower bid would forfeit labor, while raising sacrifices profit if A stays at 10.
